briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF M-019
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (-71, 17), roof
- solar canopy: (61, -100), roof
- storage hall: (-104, 128), indoor
- control room: (73, 111), indoor
- workcell West: (21, -92), indoor
- transformer pad: (-133, 65), outdoor
- water tank: (-49, 84), outdoor
- fuel depot: (75, -65), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 9 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3060 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 3 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 18 kg), camera, thermal camera. Endurance: 5340 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1200 s, including the return to its start.
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3240 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Collect a soil sample (3 kg) at fuel depot and keep it on board. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 60 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 3 kg).
- T2: Photograph control room for the condition report. Location: control room. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera.
- T3: Deliver the pressure gauge (10 kg) to control room. Location: control room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 10 kg).
- T4: Replace the filter cartridge at storage hall. Location: storage hall. Duration: 300 s. Needs: robotic arm. Deadline: finished by t = 720 s.
- T5: Deliver the replacement filter (13 kg) to workcell West. Location: workcell West. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 13 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 120 s.
- T6: Run a thermal scan of transformer pad. Location: transformer pad. Duration: 150 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 540 s.
- T7: Photograph fuel depot for the condition report. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 150 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.
- T8: Photograph storage hall for the condition report. Location: storage hall. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T9: Photograph workcell West for the condition report. Location: workcell West. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T10: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at fuel depot and keep it on board. Location: fuel depot. Duration: 120 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Morning! Plan for today's site work:

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (-71, 17, a rooftop); solar canopy (61, -100, a rooftop); storage hall (-104, 128, indoors); control room (73, 111, indoors); workcell West (21, -92, indoors); transformer pad (-133, 65, outside); water tank (-49, 84, outside); fuel depot (75, -65, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 9 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 51 minutes including getting back. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 18 kg at 3 m/s and runs for 89 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera and a thermal camera. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 9.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 20 minutes including the flight home. A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 54 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Pick up a soil sample at fuel depot and keep it on board; it weighs 3 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T2) We need pictures of control room for the report - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T3) Get the pressure gauge (10 kg) over to control room - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T4) Swap the filter cartridge at storage hall - that takes 5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 12 minutes.
(T5) Workcell West needs the replacement filter, which weighs 13 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 2 minutes.
(T6) Check transformer pad for hot spots - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 9 minutes.
(T7) We need pictures of fuel depot for the report - that takes 2.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.
(T8) Document storage hall with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T9) Document workcell West with pictures - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T10) Pick up a soil sample at fuel depot and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 2 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
